description: KIDS FUN bug-bash log (G-T39-3, Round 27). Structured findings from a manual, user-facing bug bash against STAGING (https://kids-fun-staging-jdci-nc.vercel.app, commit 761efac, backend=database), distinct from the automated regression suite (that baseline is G-T39-2). Two lanes: (a) qa-orchestrator direct HTTP/rendered-HTML/code recon of the public parent surface; (b) tester-custom real-browser exploratory pass (Chrome, desktop 1280x800 + mobile 375x812) covering parent flows, independent verification of the data-quality findings, and best-effort authed + admin console sanity on a local HEAD-0020 e2e stack (never staging). Each finding carries a severity graded on REAL USER IMPACT (not code elegance), a checkable evidence artifact, a root-cause class, and an explicit disposition. Exit-AC discipline: every critical/high finding is explicitly dispositioned (never silently deferred) — data-breadth items are ACCEPTED with rationale; confirmed code/config defects are OPEN-ROUTED-FOR-FIX (handed to the Developer for a minimal fix on a fresh branch, own test, not merged, re-QA'd before launch). qa-orchestrator is a QA conductor and does not itself write code fixes. This file is a QA log artifact, not a runtime input; the harness does not read it.

lanes.direct-recon: qa-orchestrator — HTTP + rendered-HTML + code (public parent surface)
lanes.browser-bugbash: tester-custom (sonnet) — real Chrome desktop+mobile; verified BUG-001/002; authed+admin sanity on local e2e stack; 40 screenshots at /opt/projects/crhq-satellite/images/kidsfun-r27-*.png

meta.discipline: read-mostly vs deployed staging. NOTE: the browser lane's correction-flow test wrote ONE real, contentless correction_report row to STAGING (see BUG-009) — flagged for operator cleanup; no fabricated text. Admin console eyeball used a LOCAL loopback DB admin grant only (soft-deactivated after), never staging. No secrets exposed. No core files touched.

severityScale.critical: blocks a core flow for real users; data loss/corruption; security exposure
severityScale.high: materially degrades trust or a core value-prop for real users; broken user-visible feature/link; obviously non-shippable content visible pre-launch
severityScale.medium: notable degradation or gap a user would perceive, but the flow still works

statusValues.accepted: explicitly accepted-as-known for this round (data-breadth / ingestion / curation); escalated, not a code defect
statusValues.open-routed-for-fix: confirmed code/config defect; NOT accepted as shippable; handed to the fix pipeline (Developer: fresh branch, own test, not merged, re-QA'd) — must-fix-before-launch
statusValues.deferred-logged: medium/low; logged for a future hardening round; no fix required by this task's AC
statusValues.fixed-pending-qa: was open-routed-for-fix; a minimal code fix + regression test has landed on a fresh branch (overnight/r27-g-t39-3-bugfix-bundle), NOT merged; requires independent QA re-verification before merge/launch
statusValues.qa-verified: TERMINAL. was fixed-pending-qa; independent QA re-verification PASSED with checkable artifacts — the fix is confirmed correct and cleared to ship. (Added R27 G-T39-3 independent post-merge QA lane, 2026-07-21, because the legend previously dead-ended at fixed-pending-qa with no post-QA state.)

bugs.title: Non-kid civic observances surface as kids activities
bugs.rootCauseClass: ingestion + classification (source content, not app code)
bugs.foundBy: qa-orchestrator (direct recon); CONFIRMED live in browser by tester-custom
bugs.detail: Several clearly non-kid civic/awareness observances ingested from the 'City of Vancouver events calendar' source are classified as primaryCategoryKey='class_program' (a kids-activity category) and appear in default /search results and in ANY query, including a 'toddler' search. Examples: 'International Overdose Awareness', 'National Day of Remembrance and Action on Violence Against Women', 'Remembrance Day', "Firefighters' National Memorial Day", "Police and Peace Officers' National Memorial Day". Some are somber adult topics jarring as 'fun for kids'.
bugs.userImpact: Directly undermines trust in a child-focused product. A parent browsing/filtering sees memorial days and an overdose-awareness day presented as kids activities — the kind of thing a real user notices and screenshots.
bugs.evidence: GET /api/search?limit=100 -> ~5-6 civic observances from org 'City of Vancouver events calendar' (host vancouver.ca), all class_program; also surface for q=toddler. Browser-confirmed: images/kidsfun-r27-verify-bug001.png.
bugs.resolution: ACCEPTED (not a quick app-code fix): the app renders what the pipeline classifies. Root cause is upstream source SCOPE + CLASSIFICATION QUALITY. Escalated to ingestion/classification owner (development-orchestrator). Go/no-go-material: real-source content quality is mixed.

bugs.title: Synthetic test/dev sources are live in the user-visible catalogue (example.org links)
bugs.rootCauseClass: data (test sources terms-approved into the live catalogue)
bugs.foundBy: qa-orchestrator (direct recon); CONFIRMED live in browser by tester-custom
bugs.detail: 2 of the 4 'terms-approved live sources' are clearly synthetic test fixtures: 'Age Wiring Source 945f5df0-...' (2 listings: 'Mystery Program' url=https://example.org/b, 'Baby & Me' url=https://example.org/a) and 'Venue Ingest Source 49178dac-...' (1 listing: a second 'Family Storytime', url=.../events/venue-test). Their organisation AND venueName render as the raw source UUID, and 'Official source' links point at example.org.
bugs.userImpact: A parent sees 3 listings whose 'organisation' is a UUID string and whose 'Official source' link lands on example.org (broken/fake). Obvious internal test data in the product.
bugs.evidence: GET /api/search?limit=100 -> org counts include the two UUID-named sources; sourceUrl host example.org (2). Browser-confirmed: images/kidsfun-r27-verify-bug002.png.
bugs.resolution: ACCEPTED / ESCALATED (must not be fixed by mutating staging from this read-mostly pass): recommend the operator un-approve/exclude the 2 synthetic sources before launch, OR confirm they are intentional staging-only seeds absent from production. A defensive app guard (hide example.org sources) is a workaround, not the right fix. Go/no-go-material.

bugs.title: Map view is non-functional on staging and renders an internal env-var name to end users
bugs.rootCauseClass: code + config (no map key configured for this deployment; user-facing fallback text hard-codes the env-var name)
bugs.foundBy: tester-custom (real browser); root-caused + confirmed in code by qa-orchestrator
bugs.detail: The always-visible 'Map' toggle on /search (presented as equal to 'List') never renders a map; it shows 'Map view isn't set up for this environment yet. A public Mapbox map key needs to be configured (NEXT_PUBLIC_MAP_KEY). Every result is still here — switch back to List view.' Code confirms: app/search/page.tsx:261 mapToken = (NEXT_PUBLIC_MAP_KEY ?? GEOCODING_API_KEY ?? '').trim(); neither is set on staging -> fallback in app/search/_components/ResultsMap.tsx:124-125 which literally prints NEXT_PUBLIC_MAP_KEY.
bugs.userImpact: A parent trying Map view (an advertised, equal browsing mode) hits a dead end with a technical message naming an internal env var — unprofessional to a non-technical user, and the feature is unusable as shipped on this environment. (List works and is the default, so browsing is not blocked; the impact is a broken secondary surface + a poor error message. NEXT_PUBLIC_MAP_KEY is a public-by-design var, so its NAME is not a secret leak — but it should not be shown to users.)
bugs.resolution: OPEN-ROUTED-FOR-FIX (qa is conductor, does not self-fix). Two-part recommendation for the Developer stream: (1) config — configure a Mapbox key on this deployment before any review/demo that includes Map view; or (2) code — hide/disable the Map toggle on environments where no key is present so users are never routed into the broken state, and remove the literal env-var name from any user-facing copy. Go/no-go-material (do not demo the Map view until resolved). FIX (Round 27, branch overnight/r27-g-t39-3-bugfix-bundle, NOT merged): code — the no-key fallback copy in app/search/_components/ResultsMap.tsx no longer names any env var; it now reads 'Map view isn't available right now. Every result is still here — switch back to List view.' (non-technical, no <code> element). Test tests/ui/results-map-fallback.test.tsx SSR-renders the token='' branch and asserts the markup contains neither NEXT_PUBLIC_MAP_KEY/GEOCODING_API_KEY nor any 'env var' phrasing, and still points to List view. The code path is graceful either way (real map when a key is present). CONFIG QUESTION flagged separately to the orchestrator: a 'kids-fun-mapbox' connector (KIDS FUN Mapbox/Geocoding, provider mapbox.com) DOES exist in the credential vault, but staging renders the no-key fallback — i.e. NEXT_PUBLIC_MAP_KEY is simply not wired into the staging environment. Whether to populate/wire it into staging is a deploy-config decision for the env owner (system-administrator/deploy), not assumed or wired by this fix stream; the secret value was NOT fetched or echoed.

bugs.title: Mobile: the 'Confirmed · source · Checked today' trust badge overflows the viewport, truncating on every card and detail page
bugs.area: listing cards & detail / mobile layout / core trust signal
bugs.rootCauseClass: code (CSS — the stamp element does not wrap/shrink to fit narrow viewports; extends past its container)
bugs.detail: At 375px, the green dashed '✓ Confirmed · <source> · Checked today' badge on every search-result card and on the detail page overflows the right viewport edge (badge getBoundingClientRect right=399.8 vs innerWidth=375, ~25px), cutting 'Checked today' to fragments ('Che toda' on detail; source+date clipped on cards, e.g. '✓ Confirmed · yourlibrary.bibliocomm...'). Reproduced on the first search card and on /activity/2c584a90 detail.
bugs.userImpact: This is the product's stated CORE trust mechanic (homepage: 'the source and last-checked date on every listing, so you can trust it before you go'). On mobile — plausibly the majority of real usage — that exact information is unreadable on every card and the detail page. Directly undermines the central value proposition on the primary mobile surface.
bugs.evidence: Screenshots images/kidsfun-r27-mobile-cards-badge.png, images/kidsfun-r27-mobile-detail.png. DOM: badge right=399.8px vs innerWidth=375px. (Rests on the lane's browser DOM measurement + screenshots; qa-orchestrator cannot re-measure a viewport over HTTP but accepts these as concrete checkable artifacts.)
bugs.resolution: OPEN-ROUTED-FOR-FIX. Recommend the Developer make the stamp badge wrap to a second line or ellipsis-truncate within its own box below ~400px, verified across cards + detail at 320/360/375/390px. Go/no-go-material (breaks the core trust signal on mobile). FIX (Round 27, branch overnight/r27-g-t39-3-bugfix-bundle, NOT merged): code (CSS) — app/preview/preview.css .kf-stamp now sets flex-wrap:wrap + max-width:100% so the badge wraps to a second line and never extends past its container/viewport; a new .kf-stamp__src rule (min-width:0; overflow-wrap:anywhere; word-break:break-word) lets a long source hostname break instead of pushing the row wide; a @media (max-width:400px) tune trims gap/padding/font on phones. No truncation — the full '✓ Confirmed · source · Checked today' stays readable. Test tests/ui/freshness-stamp-mobile.test.tsx asserts the CSS carries these declarations and that the source renders through the breakable .kf-stamp__src span. NOTE: vitest runs node-env (no layout engine) so true pixel-overflow at 375px must be re-measured by QA's real-browser lane at 320/360/375/390px before merge.

bugs.title: All listings render with an empty description
bugs.detail: descriptionSnippet is empty on 30/30 results, and the detail-page 'Overview' is a templated fallback ('<ActivityName> at <VenueName>.'). Confirmed on the rendered /activity/[id] page -> genuine data gap, not a card-snippet mapping bug.
bugs.userImpact: Parents scan/decide on descriptions; their absence makes every card look thin. Degrades browsing; does not break any flow.
bugs.evidence: GET /api/search?limit=100 -> empty descriptionSnippet 30/30. Rendered /activity/2c584a90 Overview = 'Family Storytime at Brighouse.'
bugs.resolution: Logged for ingestion-enrichment. Below the critical/high fix bar. Contributes to the go/no-go picture (content thinness).

bugs.title: Age data absent on ~97% of listings; age filter is effectively non-discriminating
bugs.rootCauseClass: ingestion (age bands not extracted) + by-design engine policy
bugs.detail: 29/30 listings have both ageMinMonths and ageMaxMonths null. The engine includes unknown-age listings regardless of the age filter (deliberate 'don't hide on missing data'), so filtering by age barely changes results — a 'toddler' search still returns teen clubs and civic observances. The detail page honestly discloses 'the source doesn't list an age limit', preventing a misleading answer, but the practical value of the age filter is low on current data.
bugs.userImpact: Age filtering, a headline value-prop, does little on real data. Mitigated by honest disclosure, so it is a value gap rather than a wrong-answer bug.
bugs.evidence: GET /api/search?q=toddler&limit=100 -> ctx.ageBands ['under2','2-4'] but 30 results, only 'Baby & Me' (0-36mo) ageBandMatches; rest null. Detail shows 'Ages All ages · source doesn't list an age limit'.
bugs.resolution: Logged (data-breadth-bound; same root as G-T39-2 KPI #1/#2). Ingestion age-enrichment item, not a code defect.

bugs.title: Raw region UUID rendered instead of an area name on ~30% of cards (null neighbourhood + displayArea)
bugs.rootCauseClass: code (display fallback chain uses the raw municipalityId UUID before the safe default)
bugs.foundBy: tester-custom (real browser); root-caused + quantified in code/API by qa-orchestrator
bugs.detail: app/preview/_data/search-api.ts:112 -> `l.neighbourhood ?? l.displayArea ?? l.municipalityId ?? 'Metro Vancouver'`. When neighbourhood AND displayArea are both null, the area line shows the raw municipalityId UUID '10000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000010'. Affects 9/30 visible listings (all Vancouver-citywide: the civic observances plus 'Vancouver Polar Bear Swim' and the 'Pop-up Recycling Event' cluster), on both search cards and detail pages, e.g. '10000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000010 · 13 min drive · 3.2 km'.
bugs.userImpact: ~30% of visible cards show a nonsensical database ID where a neighbourhood name should be — reads as visibly broken/unfinished.
bugs.evidence: Screenshots images/kidsfun-r27-remembranceday-card.png, images/kidsfun-r27-remembranceday-detail.png. GET /api/search?limit=100 -> 9/30 have null neighbourhood+displayArea and municipalityId=10000000-...-010; code app/preview/_data/search-api.ts:112.
bugs.resolution: OPEN-ROUTED-FOR-FIX — trivial one-line change: drop `l.municipalityId` from the fallback chain (or replace with a region-name lookup) so it never shows a raw id, falling through to 'Metro Vancouver'/'Vancouver'. Medium severity but cheap + visible on 30% of cards; recommend fixing before launch. Independent of the BUG-001 content-scope question. FIX (Round 27, branch overnight/r27-g-t39-3-bugfix-bundle, NOT merged): code — app/preview/_data/search-api.ts labelArea() now returns `l.neighbourhood ?? l.displayArea ?? 'Metro Vancouver'`, dropping l.municipalityId from the chain so a raw UUID is never rendered (no attempt to resolve the UUID to a real name — out of scope). Test tests/preview-area-label.test.ts asserts the area is 'Metro Vancouver' (never a UUID pattern) when neighbourhood+displayArea are null, and that a real neighbourhood/displayArea still wins when present.

bugs.title: 'Report wrong info' submits instantly with no confirmation and captures no reason/detail
bugs.rootCauseClass: code + product decision (no confirm step, no text-capture before the write fires)
bugs.foundBy: tester-custom (real browser); corrections contract confirmed in code by qa-orchestrator
bugs.detail: The 'Report wrong info' button on /activity|/preview/[id] has no form/text field/confirm — one click fires POST /api/corrections with body {"occurrenceId":"<id>"} (verified via network capture) and shows 'Thanks — we'll recheck this listing against the source.' There is no way to say WHAT is wrong and no undo. (Code confirms the route accepts an optional 'note' field that the UI never collects.)
bugs.userImpact: Every correction submitted site-wide is contentless, giving curators zero actionable signal beyond 'someone clicked once' — undermines the correction pipeline the product markets as part of its trust story. A misclick (easy on mobile, where the button sits above the sticky Registration/Maps bar) silently files a report with no cancel.
bugs.evidence: Screenshot images/kidsfun-r27-report-modal.png (post-click 'Thanks...' state, no form shown). Network: POST /api/corrections, postData {"occurrenceId":"2c584a90-62e5-4cc4-8fd1-2202facd4744"}, response 202.
bugs.resolution: OPEN-ROUTED-FOR-FIX (product/UX decision for Jon + a small code change): add a short reason field + a confirm step before the write. ALSO — DISCIPLINE / CLEANUP: this test click created ONE real, contentless correction_report row on STAGING against occurrenceId 2c584a90-62e5-4cc4-8fd1-2202facd4744 (Family Storytime — Brighouse). No fabricated text; harmless to leave, but an operator can dismiss it via /admin/corrections on staging if a clean queue is wanted before launch review. qa-orchestrator did not (and should not) mutate staging to remove it without proper access. FIX (Round 27, branch overnight/r27-g-t39-3-bugfix-bundle, NOT merged): code — app/preview/_components/ReportWrongInfo.tsx now gates the write behind a lightweight confirm step; the first click only shows 'Report this listing as having wrong info?' with 'Yes, report it' / 'Cancel', and the POST to /api/corrections fires ONLY on explicit confirm (Cancel returns to idle, nothing sent). The transition rule lives in an exported pure `nextReportStage` state machine so 'one click never submits' is unit-testable in this node-env project. SCOPE: per the delegated brief this fix adds the confirm gate only; the optional reason/note capture (also noted here) is left for a follow-up product decision and is out of this bundle's scope. Test tests/ui/report-wrong-info-confirm.test.tsx asserts a single 'request' yields submit=false, submission happens only after 'confirm', cancel/other transitions never submit, and the default SSR render shows the trigger (not the acknowledgement) with reportCorrection un-called. Built the confirm UI with the existing kf-link/kf-panel patterns (no new component/CSS pattern invented). NOTE: the one contentless staging correction_report row remains an operator-cleanup item (unchanged by this code fix).

bugs.title: Mobile: 'Apply dates' button overlaps the custom-date 'To' input's calendar picker
bugs.rootCauseClass: code (CSS — button not cleared below the date inputs at narrow widths)
bugs.detail: On /search at 375px, the CUSTOM DATES 'Apply dates' button overlaps the bottom-right of the 'To' date input: 'To' right edge x=217; 'Apply dates' spans x=197-296.7, y 400-436 — a ~20x36px overlap sitting over the input's native calendar-picker icon.
bugs.userImpact: A parent tapping the calendar icon on the 'To' field on a phone is likely to hit 'Apply dates' instead — fiddly, looks broken. Typing a date still works, so the flow is not blocked.
bugs.resolution: Logged for a mobile-CSS hardening pass: clear the button below the date-inputs stack on narrow viewports. Recommend bundling with BUG-011 in the same mobile-layout fix stream.

bugs.title: A recurring series can display a just-elapsed occurrence with no 'already happened' cue
bugs.detail: 'Family Storytime — Brighouse' displays a Mon Jul 20 7:30 PM occurrence (~1 day past vs today 2026-07-21) as its representative occurrence, with no 'already happened' indicator, rather than the next upcoming instance. Only 1/30; boundary case. The other 7 past-start listings are correctly-shown ongoing multi-week summer programs (future end dates).
bugs.userImpact: A single result whose shown date is ~1 day in the past. Minor, boundary-only.
bugs.evidence: GET /api/search?limit=100 -> startDatetimeUtc 2026-07-21T02:30:00Z (Jul 20 19:30 America/Vancouver). Rendered detail: 'When Mon, Jul 20 · 7:30 PM–8 PM'.
bugs.resolution: Logged for hardening: prefer next-upcoming occurrence for a recurring series, or label an elapsed one. Low, boundary case.

bugs.title: Copy/grammar nits in the zero-result empty state
bugs.foundBy: qa-orchestrator (rendered empty state); also observed by tester-custom
bugs.detail: On a zero-result search the relax-hint reads 'The search terms is the main thing narrowing your results' (subject-verb: 'terms is'), and the browse hint reads 'clear your search to browse everything on.' (awkward/possibly-truncated trailing 'on.').
bugs.userImpact: Cosmetic; a careful reader notices the grammar slip. No functional impact.
bugs.resolution: Logged as copy polish; below the fix-required bar. Fold into the next copy pass.

bugs.title: AGES/AREAS filter pills overflow with no scroll cue on desktop and mobile
bugs.foundBy: independent UX review (operator-run, uninvolved agent), Round 29
bugs.detail: AGES and AREAS filter pill rows overflow their container with no scrollbar, arrow, or fade cue on either desktop or mobile. Example: 'Richmond' gets clipped with no visible indication more options exist off-screen.
bugs.userImpact: Real discoverability bug -- a user whose area isn't in the visible pills may never realize their area is filterable at all, silently narrowing what they think is available.
bugs.evidence: Independent UX review, live production, https://kids-fun-psi.vercel.app/search.
bugs.resolution: DEFERRED-LOGGED. Not urgent, backlog for a future filter-rail hardening pass -- may be addressed alongside the Round 29 WHEN/TIME-OF-DAY redesign work (same component) if convenient, but not required for that pass's scope.

bugs.title: 'Back to today' link on activity detail pages discards the user's actual search context
bugs.foundBy: independent UX review (operator-run, uninvolved agent), Round 29
bugs.detail: The in-app 'Back to today' link on activity detail pages always routes to the generic all-listings feed regardless of how the user arrived (e.g. via a filtered/searched result), silently discarding their actual search. The real browser Back button works correctly and preserves context -- only this specific in-app link is wrong.
bugs.userImpact: A user who searched for something specific, opened a detail page, then used this link loses their search and has to redo it. Minor but a real repeated-friction annoyance.
bugs.resolution: DEFERRED-LOGGED. Backlog. Likely fix: carry the originating search's URL-encoded state through to this link the same way the app already does for shareable search URLs (existing precedent in the codebase).

bugs.title: Empty-state message has a grammar error and sometimes misattributes the cause of zero results
bugs.foundBy: independent UX review (operator-run, uninvolved agent), Round 29
bugs.detail: The zero-results empty state reads 'The search terms is...' (subject-verb agreement error). It also sometimes blames the search WORD for zero results when the real cause is the Area/Age filters narrowing the result set to nothing -- misattributing the reason to the user.
bugs.userImpact: Minor polish issue; the misattribution part is a bit more real since it could lead a user to give up on a valid search term when the actual fix is loosening a filter.
bugs.resolution: DEFERRED-LOGGED. Backlog -- two small fixes: grammar copy correction, and improving the empty-state's reasoning to check filter narrowing before blaming the query text.

bugs.title: Map view unavailable on production (informational -- confirmed pre-existing, known, accepted, not new)
bugs.foundBy: independent UX review (operator-run, uninvolved agent), Round 29 -- re-confirming a Round 27 known item, not a new finding
bugs.detail: Map view shows an honest 'Map view isn't available right now' fallback rather than rendering a map. Root cause confirmed (orchestrator, Round 29): app/search/_components/ResultsMap.tsx intentionally shows this exact fallback when no NEXT_PUBLIC_MAP_KEY token is present -- this is the SAME known, already-accepted gap logged in Round 27 (a Mapbox credential exists in the vault but was never wired into the deployed environment's NEXT_PUBLIC_MAP_KEY variable, staging or prod). Confirmed this is graceful-by-design (BUG-007 precedent: the fallback correctly reveals no env-var names or internal details to the user), not a crash or leak.
bugs.userImpact: Users who tap Map view see an honest, well-worded 'not available' message and can switch back to List. Not a broken/crashing experience, just a missing feature.
bugs.evidence: Code confirmed: app/search/_components/ResultsMap.tsx token-fallback branch. Cross-referenced against the Round 27 BUG-007 finding (evals/bugs.json).
bugs.resolution: ACCEPTED (re-confirmed, not new). Wiring NEXT_PUBLIC_MAP_KEY into the live environments (staging + the new prod project) whenever a live Map view is actually wanted remains a simple, low-risk follow-up whenever prioritized -- credential already exists in the vault (kids-fun-mapbox).
